title: Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment No 2) Bill
what_it_is: Constitution of the Republic of Singapore (Amendment No 2) Bill

sections.label: Debate on both Bills
sections.summary: Members may raise questions or views on both Bills, and the formal Second Reading of the Oaths, Declarations and Notarisations (Remote Methods) Bill will still be held.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: Members are welcome to raise questions or express their views on both Bills during the debate.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
sentences.text: We will still have the formal Second Reading of the Oaths, Declarations and Notarisations (Remote Methods) Bill to ensure that the procedural requirements are satisfied.

sections.label: Current statutory declaration process
sections.summary: Making statutory declarations, taking oaths or affirmations, and obtaining notarial acts are stringent and generally require appearing in-person before an authorised service provider.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As Members will have gathered from the brief explanation that I have given, historically, and today, the process for making a statutory declaration; taking an oath or affirmation; or obtaining a notarial act, is stringent and subject to several requirements, including the need to, generally, appear in-person before an authorised service provider, such as a Commissioner for Oaths or a Notary Public.

sections.label: Framework for remote methods
sections.summary: The Bills create a framework enabling statutory declarations, oaths and affirmations, and notarisations by electronic means while maintaining integrity and security against fraud.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Where possible, it is important that the law does not hinder, but instead supports innovation and digitalisation of business processes whilst ensuring that necessary safeguards are maintained or strengthened.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: These Bills, therefore, seek to put in place a framework that will enable statutory declarations, oaths and affirmations, and notarisations to be done through electronic means, whilst ensuring the integrity of these processes and maintaining a high degree of security against fraud.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Just to give a few recent examples, in 2021, this House enacted: (a) the Courts (Civil and Criminal Justice) Reform Act which empowered the Courts to conduct hearings remotely; (b) the Electronic Transactions (Amendment) Act, which enabled the creation and use of electronic bills of lading; and (c) the Mental Capacity (Amendment) Act, which enabled the creation and registration of electronic lasting powers of attorney.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Where a client is currently required by law and practice to appear before an authorised service provider to make a statutory declaration, take an oath, or obtain a notarial act, the framework under the Oaths, Declarations and Notarisations (Remote Methods) Bill will make it clear that the client and authorised service provider are allowed to meet using stipulated electronic means of communication.

sections.label: Electronic signatures for declarations
sections.summary: The Oaths, Declarations and Notarisations (Remote Methods) Bill provides that statutory declarations can be signed using an electronic signature.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: For statutory declarations, the Oaths, Declarations and Notarisations (Remote Methods) Bill will provide clearly that these instruments can be signed using an electronic signature.

sections.label: Past remote acts not invalidated
sections.summary: The Bill makes clear that no statutory declaration or notarial act made before the amendments is invalidated solely because video conferencing was used.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Given the lack of clarity in the current law on whether these processes can be conducted remotely, the Oaths, Declarations and Notarisations (Remote Methods) Bill will make it clear that no statutory declaration or notarial act made or carried out prior to these amendments will be invalidated solely because video conferencing was used.

sections.label: Questions on remote oaths
sections.summary: Questions are raised on preventing deep fakes and impersonations, handling power failures or network disruptions, and conditions for overseas live links.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: With the advent and advancements of artificial intelligence (AI) how do we prevent deep fakes or impersonations from compromising the integrity and validity of the oaths?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What happens if there is a power failure, a network disruption or a technical glitch for these live links?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: How do we build in contingencies in such situations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: And associated with this, will we allow overseas live links to take place and, if so, under what conditions and safeguards?

sections.label: Electronic notarial acts requirements
sections.summary: New sections 4A and 4B set requirements and criteria for notaries signing or sealing notarial acts via electronic communication such as live video link.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The new sections 4A and 4B provide for the new requirements and criteria when notaries are signing or sealing notarial acts via electronic means of communication, such as live video link.

sections.label: Commissioners for Oaths video conferencing
sections.summary: A member asks whether section 11 amendments on remote statutory declarations apply to Commissioners for Oaths or if similar rules for video conferencing are intended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For good order, may I clarify with the Senior Parliamentary Secretary, whether the proposed amendments in section 11, for the affirmation of statutory declaration by remote communications means such as video links, will apply to Commissioners for Oaths administering statutory declarations or whether there is an intention to add a similar clause to the current rules governing Commissioners for Oaths, allowing for the commissioning of affidavits via video conferencing?

sections.label: Notary jurisdiction both in Singapore
sections.summary: A notary can exercise notary jurisdiction only when the notary and the person signing are both in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Further, a notary is only able to exercise his or her jurisdiction as a notary when a notary and the relevant person signing a document before the notary are both in Singapore.

sections.label: England and Wales remote notarisation
sections.summary: It provides that the remotely located individual must be physically in England or Wales and the notary should not describe himself as an attesting witness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: For example, it provides, among other things, that "the remotely located individual must demonstrate that he or she is physically in England or Wales" and "the notary should not be considered and should not describe himself or herself as an attesting witness to the document certified by him".

sections.label: Special jurat declaratory wording
sections.summary: A possible alternative is a special jurat or prescribed wording for the signing client to declare identity and location, possibly subject to penalties for false declarations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: A possible alternative solution will be to have a special jurat or prescribed wording on the document to be executed by the signing client before the notary for the relevant person to declare and confirm his or her own identity and the location he or she was in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: Additionally, such declaratory wording by the relevant persons can even be subject to penalties for false declarations and acknowledgment of being subject to such penalties in the event of false declarations.

sections.label: Affidavits by video link
sections.summary: In April 2021 the Rules of Court were amended to allow affidavits affirmed before a Commissioner for Oaths through video or live television link, but these rules do not apply to Notaries Public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: In April 2021, the Rules of Court were amended to allow for affidavits to be affirmed by a deponent appearing before a Commissioner for Oaths through a video link or live television link.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The rules specify that the Commissioner for Oaths should be able to confirm that the person who signs the document is the person that he claims to be and that the document that he signs, together with all the exhibits attached thereto, is the same document containing the same exhibits that the Commissioner himself will later sign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: These rules, however, do not apply to oaths or other documents signed before a Notary Public.

sections.label: Parliament authorising Minister subsidiary legislation
sections.summary: Asks whether Parliament could authorise the Minister to make subsidiary legislation for virtual signing of oaths and affidavits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: For example, could the Parliament not authorise the Minister to make subsidiary legislation to allow for oaths and affidavits to be signed by a Commissioner or Notary Public to be done virtually instead of having to amend all these laws via  Parliament?

sections.label: Video link statutory declarations
sections.summary: The framework will allow statutory declarations, oaths, affirmations and notarising documents to be done over video link.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The framework will allow persons making statutory declarations, making oaths and affirmations or notarising documents to do so over video link.

sections.label: Interpreter presence for declarations
sections.summary: Asks the Senior Parliamentary Secretary to clarify whether an interpreter must be present in person with the client.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Senior Parliamentary Secretary clarify if an interpreter has to be present in person with the client making the statutory declaration, oaths or affirmations?

sections.label: Bill communication technology unspecified
sections.summary: The Bill does not specify the types of communication technology or platforms usable for the live video or television link.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Bill does not specify the types of communication technology or platforms that can be used for the live video or television link.

sections.label: Section 11 amendments CFOs
sections.summary: The answer is yes, the section 11 amendments are intended to apply to CFOs administering statutory declarations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: The answer is yes – the section 11 amendments are intended to apply to CFOs administering statutory declarations.

sections.label: Undue pressure video link requirements
sections.summary: Undue pressure is easier by video link, so the Bills set out minimum requirements the electronic link must satisfy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: It is probably easier for a person to exert undue pressure on a client in the same room without a CFO's or NP's knowledge when the CFO or NP is communicating with the client by video link instead of in-person.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: So, as mentioned earlier, the Bills set out some minimum requirements that the electronic link must satisfy.

sections.label: Electronic link requirements for service providers
sections.summary: The electronic link must let the service provider communicate with the client, confirm identity and verify documents to be signed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Specifically, the electronic link must enable the service provider to communicate with the client, confirm the client's identity and verify any document that is to be signed.

sections.label: Location requirement for statutory declarations
sections.summary: For statutory declarations and notarisations, both service provider and client must be in Singapore to rely on the ODN Bill framework.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: For statutory declarations and notarisations, both the service provider and the client must be in Singapore before they can rely on the electronic framework that is set out under the ODN Bill.

sections.label: Electronic witnessing of oaths
sections.summary: The amendments clarify that witnessing requirements for an oath can be satisfied through electronic communication such as videoconferencing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: What these amendments do, is to make clear that any witnessing requirement for an oath can also be satisfied through the use of electronic means of communication such as videoconferencing.

sections.label: Effect on DCOA and overseas Singaporeans
sections.summary: The Bills do not affect the existing position under the DCOA, and overseas Singaporeans sometimes face difficulties obtaining in-person notarial services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: These Bills do not affect the existing position under the DCOA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: We are aware overseas Singaporeans sometimes face difficulties obtaining notarial services in-person at our overseas Missions.

sections.label: Primary legislation amendments and rule-making powers
sections.summary: Amendments to primary legislation are necessary, and the Bills give the Minister rule-making powers to adjust the framework via subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: In the present case, amendments to primary legislation are necessary because we are making changes to certain requirements currently found in primary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: Nonetheless, going forward, the Bills do provide the Minister with the necessary rule-making powers to adjust the electronic framework using subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: As I have mentioned, the Minister will be able to use subsidiary legislation to prescribe specific requirements that must be satisfied.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
sentences.text: These requirements will be reviewed from time to time, to keep pace with technological developments and address new ways of committing fraud.

sections.label: Second Reading voting results
sections.summary: The voting results were 83 Ayes, zero Noes and zero Abstentions, and the Second Reading was carried by the required two-thirds majority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: So, I will proceed to declare the voting results now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There are 83 "Ayes"; zero "Noes"; zero "Abstentions".

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Second Reading of the Bill has been carried by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of Elected and Non-Constituency Members of Parliament.    .

sections.label: Third Reading vote carried
sections.summary: The Third Reading of the Bill was carried by at least two-thirds of the total Elected and Non-Constituency Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Third Reading of the Bill has been carried by the votes of not less than two-thirds of the total number of Elected and Non-Constituency Members of Parliament.
